title: Export all the BitLocker recovery information
description: Export a full report of every BitLocker volume with its recovery passwords.

windowsCommandTemplate.name: Get-BitLockerVolume
windowsCommandTemplate.commandPattern: $report = @(); Get-BitLockerVolume | ForEach-Object { $vol = $_; $_.KeyProtector | Where-Object {$_.KeyProtectorType -eq 'RecoveryPassword'} | ForEach-Object { $report += [PSCustomObject]@{ Volume=$vol.MountPoint; RecoveryPassword=$_.RecoveryPassword; KeyId=$_.KeyProtectorId } } }; $report | Export-Csv C:\BitLocker-Recovery-Report.csv -NoTypeInformation; Write-Host 'Report saved: C:\BitLocker-Recovery-Report.csv' -ForegroundColor Green

examples.command: $report = @(); Get-BitLockerVolume | ForEach-Object { $vol = $_; $_.KeyProtector | Where-Object {$_.KeyProtectorType -eq 'RecoveryPassword'} | ForEach-Object { $report += [PSCustomObject]@{Volume=$vol.MountPoint; Password=$_.RecoveryPassword} } }; $report | Format-Table
examples.description: Build a report of every recovery password

Show every property of the first object returned. Select-Object * widens the output to every column. -First 1 keeps the first result only. Use it to discover the available properties before filtering.
Show the results in a table sized for the console. Format-Table -AutoSize adjusts the column widths for readable output. Good for a quick look at structured data.
Count the objects returned. Measure-Object returns Count, Sum, Average, Min and Max depending on the properties. Useful for quick statistics and to validate results.

notes: ⚠️ CRITICAL: store this report in a secure vault (password manager, physical safe, Active Directory). NEVER send it by unencrypted email. Do NOT store it on the encrypted disk itself. Update the report after every BitLocker change.

fr.title: Exporter toutes les informations de récupération BitLocker
